articles.title: BJP Moves Motion To Remove J&K Speaker Over Omar Abdullah’s Statehood Resolution
articles.description: The Bharatiya Janata Party on Monday moved a motion seeking the removal of Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly Speaker Abdul Rahim Rather, alleging that he had allowed Chief Minister Omar Abdullah’s resolution seeking restoration of full statehood in contravention of House rules. As Assembly proceedings began, BJP legislators objected to the Speaker allowing the resolution, which was moved by Abdullah on Friday. BJP MLA RS Pathania said the party had submitted a motion seeking Rather’s removal and asked him to step aside until the matter was decided. Pathania said 23 MLAs had supported the motion and cited Rule 215(2) of the Assembly rules. He argued that the Speaker could not continue conducting proceedings while the motion was pending. ALSO READ | ‘I Am Ashamed’: NDA Ally Chirag Paswan Slams Bihar Govt Over Rising Crime, Law And Order Motion To Be Listed After 14 Days Rather rejected the BJP’s demand, saying the motion would be included in the list of business after 14 days of its submission. “You are a good lawyer. You can bring the motion. I have not seen it yet. If you read Rule 215, the procedure to be followed is laid down in the rules. A motion should be entered in the list of business any day after 14 days of submission of the motion,” Rather said. The Speaker also referred to parliamentary precedents cited by Pathania, saying those cases involved the Speaker stepping aside after the House had granted leave for the motion. “This is final,” Rather said, according to the account of proceedings. BJP MLAs continued their protest as the Speaker called for Question Hour. They raised slogans of “Kursi chodo, kursi chodo, Speaker sahab kursi chodo” and staged a sit-in in the Well of the House. Jammu, Jammu and Kashmir: Deputy CM Surinder Kumar Choudhary says, "There is no doubt that Jammu and Kashmir is not the only border area; from Rajasthan and Kutch to half of India, people live along the borders. But under the pretext that we live on the border, should we give up… pic.twitter.com/6iD7bKf7Df — IANS (@ians_india) September 28, 2026 BJP Objects To Statehood Resolution The confrontation came as the Assembly took up discussion on Abdullah’s resolution seeking the “immediate and urgent restoration of full statehood” to Jammu and Kashmir. The resolution also refers to resolutions passed by the House in June 2000 and November 2024. The reference to the 2000 resolution, which had sought greater autonomy for Jammu and Kashmir, has become a major point of contention between the BJP and the ruling parties. BJP legislators have argued that references to autonomy and the pre-1953 constitutional position should not form part of the debate. Leader of Opposition Sunil Sharma said references to the pre-1953 position and autonomy were unacceptable. He also pointed out that the BJP had opposed the 2000 autonomy resolution when Abdullah was a Union minister. ALSO READ | CJP's Ashutosh Ranka Hits Back At CM Himanta Sarma After Release From Detention Amendments Seek References To Articles 370, 35A The statehood resolution has also attracted several amendments from legislators seeking to expand its scope. Amendments moved by members of the National Conference and other parties seek references to the restoration of Articles 370 and 35A. PDP MLA Waheed Para separately moved an amendment seeking restoration of the provisions in their original form. According to the Jammu and Kashmir Assembly’s official portal, a list of amendments to Abdullah’s resolution was circulated ahead of Monday’s proceedings. Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Choudhary said Union Home Minister Amit Shah had promised restoration of statehood on the floor of the House three years ago, but the commitment had not yet been fulfilled. Health Minister Sakeena Itoo, meanwhile, pointed to the BJP’s participation in the 2000 autonomy resolution debate and said that this aspect should also be reported. The BJP has opposed the current resolution and questioned both its contents and the Speaker’s handling of the proceedings. The dispute has led to repeated disruptions in the Assembly as the House debates the demand for restoration of Jammu and Kashmir’s full statehood.

articles.title: Breaking News: SIR Row Intensifies as EC Eases Process, BJP CMs Gear Up to Counter Opposition
articles.description: The controversy surrounding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) has entered a new phase, with political tensions escalating across the country. Opposition parties have intensified their attack on Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar , even demanding his removal and legal action. Amid the growing row, a key opposition alliance meeting is also being planned to strategize the next steps. In a significant development, BJP-ruled states are preparing a coordinated response. Several Chief Ministers, including Yogi Adityanath , are set to hold press conferences to counter allegations and present the government’s stance. The move signals a unified political pushback against the opposition narrative. Meanwhile, the Election Commission held its first full meeting amid the controversy, attended by Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi . The Commission announced key reforms to simplify the SIR process. Under the revised system, Booth Level Officers (BLOs) will visit voters’ homes to collect documents, eliminating the need for citizens to visit ERO or AERO offices. Documents will be uploaded on-site, and decisions will be taken by EROs. The Commission has also introduced flexibility by allowing voters to authorize an adult family member for hearings. Help desks and special camps will be set up, particularly to assist migrants, homeless individuals, and economically weaker sections. Additionally, Form 6 under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 will continue for regular voter registration outside the SIR period. Deadlines for claims and objections have been extended in Delhi and Maharashtra, reflecting an effort to ensure wider participation. While the Commission maintains that decisions were unanimous, political reactions remain divided, keeping the issue at the center of national debate.

articles.title: Breaking News: Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma Hits Out at Rahul Gandhi Over EC Controversy
articles.description: In a sharp escalation of the political battle over the Election Commission controversy, Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma launched a fierce attack on the opposition, particularly targeting Rahul Gandhi and the Congress ecosystem. Sarma accused opposition leaders of deliberately misleading the public by claiming divisions within the Election Commission regarding the Special Investigation Review (SIR) process and Form 6-related decisions. Referring to the Commission’s recent clarification, Sarma emphasized that all decisions taken by the full bench were based on consensus, with no internal disagreements. He stated that the narrative of “difference of opinion” was artificially created and amplified across the country without evidence. According to him, this misinformation campaign not only undermined the credibility of the Election Commission but also eroded public trust in democratic institutions. The Assam Chief Minister further alleged that certain groups, which he described as aligned with the Congress ecosystem, fueled the controversy by demanding a rollback of the SIR process and even calling for the resignation of Election Commission officials. Sarma questioned whether Rahul Gandhi and his supporters would now apologize to the nation in light of the Commission’s clarification. The remarks have added fresh intensity to the ongoing political debate, with the ruling side accusing the opposition of irresponsible rhetoric, while opposition leaders continue to raise concerns about transparency and electoral processes. As the controversy unfolds, the issue is likely to remain a flashpoint in national politics, especially with key elections approaching.
